item.title: Nonpolar Micro‐Environment‐Induced Solvation Field Engineering Enables 600 Wh Kg −1 High‐Voltage Lithium Metal Pouch Cells
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a nonpolar micro-environment-induced electrolyte using propyl propionate as an amphiphilic inducer to engineer the Li+ solvation field at conventional salt concentration, driving contact-ion-pair-dominated solvation. This decouples interfacial stability from ion transport, enabling a 604 Wh kg−1 Li||NCM95 pouch cell, 87.7% retention over 200 cycles in a 4.2 Ah cell, and −20°C graphite operation—a new principle for high-energy battery electrolytes.
🏷 lithium metal battery · solvation field · electrolyte design · pouch cell · high voltage

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in combining hierarchical pore confinement with Ni-catalyzed iodine conversion via d–p orbital interactions in self-standing Ni@CNBs-CMF cathodes. This synergy suppresses the iodine shuttle effect, enabling 16,000-cycle life, 90% Coulombic efficiency after 168-h rest, and 382.8 mAh g⁻¹ via the I⁻/I⁰/I⁺ pathway—significantly advancing practical aqueous Zn–I₂ batteries for large-scale energy storage.
🏷 Zn-I2 battery · iodine shuttle · Ni nanoparticles · carbon fibers · catalytic conversion

item.description:

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in a "nano-friction-strengthening" strategy: core-shell nanoparticles in a carbonate-swollen shell activate dynamic hydrogen bonds under impact, boosting interparticle friction and viscosity 160-fold for impact hardening. This cuts impact force by 73.1%, preventing short circuits in pouch cells, while phosphate-ester groups suppress thermal runaway, enabling safer lithium metal batteries under mechanical abuse.
